solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Promising European's no good before finally getting on

indicators.note: before says the first pieces come ahead of what follows

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European
someone getting on in years is ageing, here spelt without the middle E

explanation.surface: A European with nothing going for them finally manages to get along with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' is padding in the surface; 'getting on' means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Something promising is attractive and appealing, a close synonym of charming or winning.

clue.text: Aerosol, regularly returned, containing unknown leak

indicators.note: containing means the reversed letters hold the next piece inside them
returned means the picked letters are read backwards
regularly picks every other letter of the word aerosol, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A spray can, sent back again and again, has a mysterious leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Aerosol are E, O, O; 'returned' turns them to OOE, and Z goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to seep out slowly, the way a liquid escapes through a small opening.

clue.text: Can I run after, ultimately, one more minute?

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word one

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner asks whether they can chase down one more minute in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places R after the last letter of 'one'; 'minute' is the adjective (my-NEWT), not the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute as an adjective means very small, so more minute is smaller still.

clue.text: Leaderless group occupying ridge turned up for more of the same

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
occupying means the shortened group sits inside the ridge

parts.note: an arete is a sharp mountain ridge

indicators.note: leaderless means the word for group loses its first letter

parts.note: a sect is a group of believers

explanation.surface: A band of climbers without a guide camp on a ridge that has been heaved upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: ECT goes inside ARETE to give ARETECTE, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for 'and the rest' signals that further similar items follow.

clue.text: Left after coaches roll up, missing one UN employee?

indicators.note: after puts the letter for left behind the shortened coaches
missing means the trains lose the letter standing for one

parts.note: coaches train athletes, so the verb trains
the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the rota is written bottom to top

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a rota

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed behind when the coaches pulled away, missing one employee of the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAINS without I gives TRANS; ROTA reversed by 'up' is ATOR. The question mark flags that translators are only one kind of UN employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpreters and translators are prominent staff at the United Nations, rendering speeches across official languages.

clue.text: Bully for hero

definitions.meaning: to bully is to browbeat or intimidate someone
the Trojan champion killed by Achilles in the Iliad

explanation.surface: Someone cheering on a playground tough instead of a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to harass with bluster; the name belongs to the greatest warrior of Troy.

clue.text: Civil warmonger, possibly in situ, on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A warlike figure is spotted on the spot, out on army exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Civil warmonger' is a whimsical way of saying a fighter in the American Civil War; the federal side were known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the North in the American Civil War fought to preserve the federal union.

clue.text: Most excellent dope? Mine, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so both words are reversed

parts.note: dope is slang for cannabis, also called pot
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their drugs and their mining venture are, thinking about it, first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: POTPIT read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal adjective describes something of the very highest quality, first-class.

clue.text: Mark pressed endlessly to stop tasteless articles

indicators.note: to stop means the trimmed word plugs the gap in the middle of the junk

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for pressed loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: pressed in the sense of urged someone on

explanation.surface: A mark pressed onto cheap trinkets without end to put a stop to their sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both ends of the word for pressed, and 'to stop' plugs the result into the junk like a cork. 'Mark' here is the thing aimed at.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark can be the thing aimed at, such as a bullseye or an objective.

clue.text: Ambassador hiding form of blackjack that's fishy

indicators.note: hiding means the ambassador's letters wrap around the card letters

parts.note: HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
an ace and a king make 21, a winning blackjack hand: A and K

explanation.surface: A diplomat concealing a card-game cheat looks suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: In blackjack an ace with a king is a natural 21, so the hand is written AK.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a sea creature, so as a fish it is literally fishy.

clue.text: Saturate using permeating fluid

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so these letters are poured into a new order

explanation.surface: Soak something through with a liquid that seeps in everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to fill or soak something thoroughly, permeating it completely.

clue.text: Take something from Karachi, thereupon to this place

indicators.note: take something from says the letters are lifted out of the run of text that follows

explanation.surface: Someone collects goods in Pakistan's port city and then brings them back here.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning towards the speaker, as in come over here.

clue.text: Clinic admitting bishop, English kind

indicators.note: admitting means the hospital lets the bishop's letter in

parts.note: a clinic is a medical place, a hospital
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A medical clinic takes in an English bishop as a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes in between the A and L of HOSPITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind host is welcoming and generous to guests, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Ruler put too much weight on introducing small change

indicators.note: a small change alters just one letter of the word for overburden

parts.note: to load beyond capacity is to overload

explanation.surface: A monarch piles on too many pounds, bringing in a little loose coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: One letter of OVERLOAD is swapped: its A becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme lord or feudal superior who rules over lesser lords.

clue.text: Try small drink. It's the same as …

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: An invitation to taste a tiny drink, linked to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into 17 across: this answer is the same as the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter about others' affairs, the same meaning as the next answer, tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Begin, leader of Israeli province, I introduced to gallery

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word Israeli

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

indicators.note: introduced to means the I is put inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: An Israeli leader of a province makes their debut at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province'. The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in motion is to start it off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: … this. Cheers! Name but one

parts.note: ta is a British informal word for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: but here means except, so the title is taken without one letter

parts.note: a title is a name
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A toast is raised, then someone names all but one person present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers back to the answer of 15 across, so the answer means the same as gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter spread about other people, the same thing as the previous answer.

clue.text: It's used to highlight orbital boundaries

definitions.text: It's used to highlight orbital boundaries

parts.words: It's used to highlight orbital boundaries
parts.note: orbital suggests space or planets, but the orbit here is the eye socket, and the borders made more visible are the lids

explanation.surface: Something like a space beacon marking the edges of a satellite's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbital' pretends to be about astronomy but refers to the eye socket, the orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic drawn along the lids to accentuate the edges of the eyes.

clue.text: In heaven after working more than normal

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
high means above the usual level

explanation.surface: Someone is in bliss after doing overtime at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up above in the sky, the traditional abode of God.

clue.text: System for firing one caught in observing another one from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the whole thing is read from the back
caught in means the first one sits trapped inside the word for observing

parts.note: noting is observing
the Roman numeral I is one
a second I, again the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone describes a firing system: one person caught watching another from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: I inside NOTING gives NOITING; adding I and reading 'from behind' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In an engine, this is the mechanism that sparks the fuel to start combustion.

clue.text: Guiding spirit involved with, say, rising states

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the two pieces are read upwards

parts.note: to be in on something is to be involved with it
eg, for example, is what say means here
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A guiding spirit is implicated, so to speak, in nations on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses only the first two pieces, giving GENI; 'states' is not reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman belief a protective spirit attended each person or place, the original sense of the word.

clue.text: This stone is converted into inert gas

indicators.note: converted into says the letters of the stone plus the word is are remade as the phrase inert gas

explanation.surface: A gemstone is turned into a noble gas, like alchemy in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: the answer plus IS rearranges to make INERT GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red semi-precious gemstone, often used in jewellery.

clue.text: Jumble sale getting half-reduced clothing up front

indicators.note: up front means the clothing goes at the start

parts.note: garb is clothing

indicators.note: half-reduced keeps only the back half of the word sale

explanation.surface: A jumble sale gets cut-price clothes displayed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble sale' reads as one thing, but 'Jumble' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble is to mix up or distort a message so it is confused.

clue.text: Strange, regularly funny friend

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of funny, the second and fourth

parts.note: a familiar is an intimate friend or companion

explanation.surface: A pal who is always a bit odd and comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not known before seems odd or novel, hence strange.

clue.text: Bird's limited visibility to the west

indicators.note: to the west in an across clue means the letters run leftwards, backwards
limited says only part of the word visibility is used

explanation.surface: A bird has poor eyesight looking westward.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Smooth man, one taking the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means the letter for one goes in front

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A suave man, one who steps up to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' looks like an adjective describing the man, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To press creases out of clothes with a hot appliance is to make them smooth.

clue.text: Old unopened bit of meat market

indicators.note: unopened means the meat loses its first letter

parts.note: a cutlet is a small piece of meat

explanation.surface: A stale, unwrapped piece of meat on sale at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail outlet is a shop or market where goods are sold.

clue.text: Postpone start of holidays, taking early deliveries

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the word holidays

parts.note: old in the sense of from an early period, as in olden times
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Someone delays the beginning of a holiday because some packages arrived early.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls, each called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer a matter to a later date is to put it off, a synonym of postpone.
